articles.title: Aurora supercomputer powers two of the largest cosmological simulations to date
articles.description: Researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory have completed two of the largest cosmological simulations ever performed. Each simulation modeled the evolution of 13.4 trillion dark matter particles across a region 28.6 billion light-years wide.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Aurora supercomputer at Argonne National Laboratory has completed two of the largest cosmological simulations to date, enabling researchers to model the universe's structure and evolution with unprecedented precision. These simulations represent a major breakthrough in computational astrophysics.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Astronomers have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the universe's earliest moments by measuring cosmic composition during the first five minutes after the Big Bang. This achievement provides unprecedented insights into primordial nucleosynthesis and the universe's fundamental origins.

articles.title: Two monster black holes could collide in just 100 years
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, with observations suggesting the pair completes an orbit every 121 days. Depending on their masses, these cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward each other, with a potential collision occurring within just 100 years. This extraordinary discovery represents one of the most significant cosmic events expected in our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
articles.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe. By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
articles.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded performance expectations by nearly 30% following precision engineering adjustments. This major achievement promises enhanced capabilities for future astronomical observations.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the first-ever detection of a microblazar, a new class of compact astronomical object distinct from traditional blazars. This groundbreaking discovery expands our understanding of cosmic particle acceleration phenomena.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen and the IceCube neutrino observatory win the 2026 Physics Nobel Prize for detecting high-energy neutrinos from space. This landmark achievement opens a new window into understanding the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: Zehn Gramm sollen auf die Erde geholt werden – spektakuläre Mars-Mond-Mission gestartet
articles.description: Japan möchte Bodenproben vom Mars-Mond Phobos holen und hat eine Sonde auf den Weg geschickt. Deutschland ist am Rover Idefix beteiligt, der mit nur 15 Gramm Gewicht funktionieren soll.
articles.summary: Japan launches an ambitious spacecraft mission to collect soil samples from Phobos, Mars's mysterious moon, with German partnership.

articles.title: Japan launches spacecraft to mysterious moons of Mars in a bold mission to bring home soil samples
articles.description: Japan launches spacecraft to mysterious moons of Mars in a bold mission to bring home soil samplesclickondetroit.com
articles.summary: Japan's bold spacecraft mission to the moons of Mars aims to return the first-ever soil samples from the Red Planet's mysterious satellites.

articles.title: Japan leads mission to make first return trip to Mars
articles.description: Voyage due to launch early Tuesday morning Japan time will be watched for further potential signs of life on red planet
articles.summary: Japan leads an unprecedented mission to return samples from Mars, opening new possibilities for discovering signs of life on the Red Planet.

articles.summary: Japan's MMX mission successfully launches toward Mars's moon Phobos to explore and collect samples from this mysterious Martian satellite.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope makes an exciting discovery of a previously unknown comet, demonstrating the power of modern astronomical surveys.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA's Solar Orbiter spacecraft unveils the mysteries of magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, revealing new insights into solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures stunning images of energetic stellar jets within a nebula, revealing the violent and creative process of star formation.

articles.title: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration Mission is on its Way to Mars and Phobos
articles.description: JAXA successfully launched its Martian Moon eXplorer on its way to Mars and Phobos. It'll reach Mars in about six months, and will orbit the planet for about a month before transferring to an orbit around Phobos. It will deploy a small lander, which will help select a sample-gathering location for the main part of the mission. By 2031, the regolith sample from Phobos should be back on Earth.
articles.summary: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration mission successfully launches toward Mars and Phobos, with arrival expected in approximately six months.

articles.title: The Gas Near Sagittarius A-star is Enriched in Metals, Probably from Supernovae Explosions
articles.description: The region near Sagittarius A-star, the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, is enriched in metals, although only modestly. The likely cause is supernovae explosions, which synthesize elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Over time, this metal-rich gas found its way towards the SMBH. The increased metallicity and heat from the supernova affect how fast gas flows into the SMBH.
articles.summary: Observations reveal that the gas surrounding Sagittarius A*, the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, is enriched with metals from ancient supernovae explosions.

articles.title: A Magnetar Can Be Born When Two Neutron Stars Touch
articles.description: Magnetars are neutron stars with magnetic fields a thousand times stronger than normal. One way that magnetars might form is through the merger of two small neutron stars.
articles.summary: Scientists discover that magnetars—neutron stars with extraordinarily powerful magnetic fields—can form when two neutron stars merge and interact.

articles.title: JWST Tracks Shifting Water Clouds and Churning Gases on the Coldest Known Brown Dwarf
articles.description: When picturing a star, typically people think of giant balls of burning gas in the sky that emit enough light they are hard to miss. Planets, on the other hand, come in one of two general categories - rocky worlds like Earth or gas giants similar to Jupiter. But there is a third category of astronomical object that doesn’t really fit either of those descriptions, and also doesn’t exist in our own solar system. Known as a brown dwarf, they are sometimes called a “failed star” as they form the same way stars do, but never reach the critical mass of material to create active fusion in the cores. They are also much too massive to be considered a regular planet. But a new paper from researchers led by Brittany Miles of the University of Arizona describes one similarity between the coldest known brown dwarf and some of the planets in our solar system - it has water-ice clouds.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope observes dynamic water clouds and churning atmospheric gases on the coldest known brown dwarf, expanding our understanding of substellar objects.

articles.title: Webb Captures This Golden Galaxy Cluster in All it's Glory
articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features the brilliant golden galaxies belonging to the MACS J0454.1-0300 galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a breathtaking image of a brilliant golden galaxy cluster, showcasing the cosmos's magnificent beauty and scale.

articles.title: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope Has Discovered A New Comet
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid space telescope was launched in July, 2026, and its mission is to observe billions of galaxies. The goal is to measure their redshifts over 10 billion years of Universal expansion, to better understand dark matter and dark energy. Surprisingly, the telescope has discovered a brand new comet, now named C/2026 S1 (Euclid).
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope, launched in July 2026, has discovered a new comet while conducting its mission to observe billions of galaxies. This discovery demonstrates the telescope's capability to detect unexpected celestial objects during its cosmological survey.

articles.title: Water as we've never known it: Physicists test water beyond Earth-like conditions
articles.description: Water isn't always as it seems. Under extreme conditions, such as those found on other planets, it has been discovered to change its atomic structure, giving it the means to alter its appearance and other properties.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered that water behaves dramatically differently under extreme conditions found on other planets, revealing new insights into planetary chemistry and composition. This research expands our understanding of potential environments for discovering water-based worlds.

articles.title: A pulsar's apparent slowdown reveals a rare stellar trio
articles.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars, the extremely dense cores left behind when massive stars explode. Astrophysicists have recently observed a pulsar rotating over 300 times per second that appeared to be slowing down unusually quickly.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astrophysicists have discovered a rare stellar trio system by detecting a pulsar's apparent slowdown, revealing a complex gravitational dance between rapidly rotating neutron stars. This discovery provides new insights into extreme stellar systems and neutron star physics.

articles.title: NASA experimental Mars helicopter blade designs target longer flights
articles.description: NASA researchers are developing the future of flight on Mars, laying the groundwork for helicopters with the ability to fly higher and farther while conducting science on the Red Planet. Using high-fidelity computer simulations and wind tunnel tests, engineers are reimagining the rotorcraft blades that could carry the next generation of Mars flyers.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA researchers are developing advanced helicopter blade designs that will enable longer, more ambitious flights on Mars, paving the way for expanded aerial exploration of the Red Planet. These innovations represent a major step toward sustained atmospheric operations on Mars.

articles.title: Hot plasma may explain how rapidly feeding black holes launch powerful jets
articles.description: Some supermassive black holes rapidly consume surrounding matter while simultaneously firing powerful streams of plasma into space at nearly the speed of light. However, this creates a physical puzzle: rapid feeding is expected to form a cold, flat accretion disk around the black hole, which prevents powerful jets from forming.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that hot plasma may explain how rapidly feeding supermassive black holes launch their powerful relativistic jets into space. This research reveals fundamental mechanisms governing black hole behavior and energy output.

articles.title: Giant canyon on Mars is still tectonically active today
articles.description: Scientists at Columbia University and Imperial College London have found that the largest canyon system in the solar system is still active and shaping Mars today, billions of years after it first formed.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have found that Mars's Valles Marineris, the largest canyon system in the solar system, remains geologically active today with ongoing tectonic processes. This discovery demonstrates that Mars continues to evolve dynamically despite its cold, barren surface.

articles.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
articles.description: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders. Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years.
articles.summary: NASA scientists have solved the mystery of why asteroid Bennu loses heat so rapidly despite being covered in massive boulders, revealing unexpected thermal properties of the asteroid. This discovery from NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission enhances our understanding of asteroid composition and behavior.

articles.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
articles.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.
articles.summary: NASA has released a stunning gallery of 16 galaxies showcasing cosmic phenomena including colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular galactic structures. These images reveal the dynamic and energetic processes occurring throughout the universe.

articles.title: A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon aboard a rover named FLIP
articles.description: And yes, it has AI.
articles.summary: An AI-powered supercomputer is preparing to launch to the moon aboard the FLIP rover, representing a major leap in autonomous lunar exploration technology. This mission combines advanced computing with robotic lunar exploration capabilities.

articles.title: SpaceX launches its 'Starfall' return capsule for 2nd time ever (video)
articles.description: SpaceX launched its Starfall return capsule for the second time ever this morning (Oct. 20), sending it up on the Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission.
articles.summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starfall return capsule for the second time, demonstrating progress toward reusable spacecraft technology. This milestone advances the goal of efficient and sustainable space transportation.

articles.title: Astronomers Uncover More Intriguing Detail in an Ancient Supernova Remnant
articles.description: When a supernova exploded in 1181, Chinese and Japanese sky-watchers recorded it. They couldn't have known what the object was, and why it appeared for six months then disappeared. But in our modern times, we know it was a supernova, and we've even, most like…
articles.summary: Astronomers have uncovered new details in an ancient supernova remnant from the 1181 explosion recorded by Chinese and Japanese observers. Modern analysis of this historical event continues to reveal insights into stellar explosions and cosmic evolution.

articles.title: CHIME time, AI transparency in research, ‘Evolution’ on PBS, and faculty honors
articles.description: Yale researchers help prove the utility of an innovative radio telescope in understanding the expanding universe and offer thoughts on how to best use AI in science. Meanwhile, faculty members in physics and astronomy are honored for breakthroughs across an a…
articles.summary: Yale researchers validate the innovative CHIME radio telescope's capability to advance our understanding of the expanding universe.
